name: Queen's Gambit
summary: White offers the c-pawn to pull Black's d-pawn away from the center. It is less a real gambit than a fight for the e4 square and the open c-file. The ideas are classical: develop quickly, claim the center, and build pressure slowly.

chunks.title: Introduction & Main Line
chunks.summary: The core move order 1.d4 d5 2.c4 and why it works: White attacks the d5 pawn from the side and asks Black how they want to defend the center.
keyIdeas: 2.c4 attacks d5 from the side. If Black takes, White can usually win the pawn back with e3 and Bxc4.
Against 2...e6 the natural development is Nc3, Nf6 and Bg5, which piles pressure on d5.
White's long-term plans are the minority attack (b4–b5), a central e4 break, or play on the half-open c-file.

line.note: Claims the center and frees the c1 bishop. The queen already protects d4.
The classical reply. Black matches White in the center.
The Queen's Gambit. It challenges d5 without blocking the c-pawn with a knight.
The Queen's Gambit Declined. Black backs up d5 but shuts in the c8 bishop.
More pressure on d5. White develops toward the center.
Black defends d5 a third time and gets ready to castle.
Pins the f6 knight, which is one of d5's defenders.

questions.prompt: You're White. Start the Queen's Gambit.
questions.hint: Push a center pawn that the queen already protects.
questions.explanation: 1.d4 takes space, opens the c1 bishop and starts every Queen's Gambit.

questions.prompt: Black matched you in the center. Offer the gambit.
questions.hint: Hit d5 from the side with a flank pawn.
questions.explanation: 2.c4 attacks d5 without blocking the c-pawn. If Black takes, White usually wins the pawn back with e3 and Bxc4.

questions.prompt: Black declined the gambit with 2...e6. Which developing move adds pressure to d5?
questions.explanation: 3.Nc3 is the main line. The knight hits d5 and prepares Bg5. 3.Nf3 is also good and more flexible.

chunks.title: Queen's Gambit Accepted
chunks.summary: Black takes on c4 and gives up the center for a while in exchange for free development. White's job is to win the pawn back calmly and keep a central advantage.
keyIdeas: Don't hurry to win back c4. e3 and Bxc4 get it back, because Black cannot safely hold the pawn.
White's bishop lands on c4 with tempo, aimed at f7 and the center.
Black's typical plan is ...c5 and ...a6–b5. White answers by castling and thinking about Qe2, Rd1 and a central e4 push.

line.note: The Accepted. Black gives up the center to develop freely.
Stops ...e5 and develops. White isn't worried about the c4 pawn yet.
Natural development. It also keeps White from playing e4 for free.
Opens the f1 bishop, which gets ready to take on c4.
The pawn is back. White has a central edge and an active bishop.
Black's standard central counter-strike.
King to safety first. The tension in the center can wait.
Prepares ...b5 to kick the bishop.

questions.prompt: Black accepted the gambit. What's the most flexible developing move?
questions.hint: Develop a knight that also stops ...e5.
questions.explanation: 3.Nf3 develops and stops ...e5. 3.e3 and 3.e4 are also main lines. The c4 pawn will come back.

questions.prompt: Time to collect the gambit pawn.
questions.hint: The light-squared bishop now has a path to c4.
questions.explanation: 5.Bxc4 wins the pawn back and puts the bishop on its best diagonal. White keeps a small central edge.

questions.prompt: Black hits your center with ...c5. What's the calm, principled reply?
questions.explanation: 6.O-O finishes the kingside setup. Taking on c5 or locking the center too early only helps Black.

chunks.title: Declined: Orthodox Defense
chunks.summary: Black keeps a solid pawn on d5 with ...e6, ...Be7 and ...Nbd7. White develops for maximum pressure and fights over the c4 square and the c-file.
keyIdeas: Bg5 pins the f6 knight, which is one of d5's defenders.
The fight for a tempo. White plays useful moves like Rc1 before Bd3, because Black wants to take on c4 only once the bishop has moved.
Watch out for the Elephant Trap. The d5 pawn often looks loose when it isn't (see Traps).

line.note: The pin. White now threatens to win d5 by taking on f6.
Breaks the pin and gets ready to castle.
Solid. Protects d4 and opens the f1 bishop.
The Orthodox setup. Black supports ...c5 or ...e5 later.
A useful waiting move. It aims at the c-file before Black plays ...c5.
Black can now take on c4, but White wins it back in one move.
White keeps a small but lasting edge thanks to the extra space.

questions.prompt: Black defends d5 with the knight. Put pressure on that defender.
questions.hint: Pin the f6 knight to the queen.
questions.explanation: 4.Bg5 pins the knight that guards d5. That defines the classical Orthodox lines.

questions.prompt: Both sides are developing. Bring out your last minor piece.
questions.hint: The kingside knight is still at home.
questions.explanation: 6.Nf3 is the main line. It finishes minor-piece development and supports d4 and e5.

questions.prompt: Black finally took on c4. Restore material.
questions.hint: Win the pawn back without losing a tempo.
questions.explanation: 9.Bxc4. This is the classic fight for a tempo. Black waited until Bd3 to take, so the bishop moves twice. White's useful Rc1 makes up for it, and the small space edge stays.

chunks.title: Slav Defense
chunks.summary: Black defends d5 with ...c6, which keeps the c8 bishop free to develop. White plays a4 to stop ...b5, wins back c4, and aims for e4.
keyIdeas: After ...dxc4, Black wants to hold the pawn with ...b5. 5.a4 stops that for good.
Black's main development is ...Bf5, putting the bishop outside the pawn chain before ...e6.
White's bishop wins back c4. Then the plan is e3, O-O, Qe2 and a central break with e4.

line.note: The Slav. It supports d5 without shutting in the c8 bishop.
Now Black takes and hopes to hold the pawn with ...b5.
Stops ...b5 for good. The c4 pawn is now weak.
The point of the Slav. The bishop comes out before ...e6.
Material is level, and White has a central majority.
Pins the c3 knight to make e4 harder.
Next comes Qe2 and e4 to break open the center.

questions.prompt: The Slav. What's the most flexible developing move?
questions.explanation: 3.Nf3 develops while keeping options open. It also covers e5 and d4.

questions.prompt: Black took on c4 and wants to hold it with ...b5. Stop that plan.
questions.hint: A rook-pawn move puts a stop to ...b5.
questions.explanation: 5.a4 takes away ...b5. The c4 pawn can't be held, and White will win it back with Bxc4.

questions.prompt: Collect the pawn and develop with tempo.
questions.hint: e3 opened a diagonal for your bishop.
questions.explanation: 7.Bxc4 wins the pawn back. White has an easy game with O-O, Qe2 and e4 to come.

chunks.title: Traps & Pitfalls
chunks.summary: Two classic traps. One punishes Black for greedily holding the gambit pawn. The other is a trap White must not fall into when d5 looks loose.
keyIdeas: If Black holds c4 with ...b5, a4 undermines the chain. Then Qf3 uses the long diagonal to hit the a8 rook.
The Elephant Trap: after cxd5 exd5, Nxd5?? loses to ...Nxd5!, because Bxd8 is met by ...Bb4+ and Black comes out a piece ahead.
Pins work both ways. Before you grab a pawn, check whether your own pieces are overloaded.

line.note: Greedy. Black tries to hang on to the c4 pawn.
Hits the base of the pawn chain right away.
The long diagonal f3–a8 is open. The rook on a8 and the knight on b8 can't both be saved.

questions.prompt: Black is trying to keep the extra pawn with ...b5. Punish it.
questions.hint: Attack the b5 pawn, the base of the chain.
questions.explanation: 4.a4 undermines the b5–c4 chain at once. Black's queenside starts to come apart.

questions.prompt: Black's queenside pawns have gone. Find the move that wins material.
questions.hint: Look at the long light-squared diagonal toward a8.
questions.explanation: 6.Qf3! hits the a8 rook along the open diagonal. Black has to give up material, for example 6...Nc6 7.Qxc6+.

questions.prompt: d5 looks like it's hanging because the f6 knight is pinned. Is it? Play the correct move.
questions.hint: Don't take on d5. Just keep developing.
questions.explanation: 6.e3! The Elephant Trap is 6.Nxd5?? Nxd5! 7.Bxd8 Bb4+ 8.Qd2 Bxd2+ 9.Kxd2 Kxd8, and Black is a piece up. The pin on f6 isn't real.
